draft.title: Supply
card: Supply is how much of a product sellers will offer for sale at each price.
As the price rises, sellers usually offer more. A higher price means more money for each item sold.
As the price falls, sellers usually offer less. Some items may no longer be worth making at a low price.
Supply is about sellers. It is different from demand, which is about what buyers want and can afford.
draft.remember: Higher price, more offered for sale. Lower price, less offered.

opts: How much sellers will offer at each price
How much buyers want to buy at each price
How much a product costs to make
How many sellers there are in a market
a.why: Supply is the amount sellers will offer at each price. The option about buyers describes demand, which is a different idea.
a.clue: Supply is about the sellers' side of the market.

b.q: The price of strawberries at a Tasmanian farm gate rises from $4 to $6 a punnet. What will the farm usually do?
opts: Offer more punnets for sale
Offer fewer punnets for sale
Offer the same number of punnets
Stop selling to buyers
b.why: A higher price means more income for each punnet, so sellers usually offer more. Offering fewer would match a price fall, not a rise.
b.clue: What does a higher price mean for the seller's income?

a.best: How much sellers will offer at each price

problems.detail: The last bullet restates demand's definition ('what buyers want and can afford'), which belongs to point 1. It would be enough to mention that supply is different from demand.
The remember line drops the card's 'usually' ('Higher price, more offered for sale'), so it reads as a rule that always holds.
